newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-PREMIER LEAGUE TO DECIDE ON WHEN SEASON TO END.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PREMIER LEAGUE TO DECIDE ON WHEN SEASON TO END.

text.p: The premier league will rule this week on whether the English soccer season is to be extended and put an end to a feud involving the country's top managers.
Manchester United boss Alex Ferguson is calling for the extension to ease a fixture pile-up as his side chase a premier league and European Cup double.
But Arsenal's Arsene Wenger is against the move and earned the wrath of Ferguson at the weekend for voicing his opinion.
Then Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson joined the fray, backing his former Old Trafford boss, while Liverpool's Roy Evans sided with Wenger.
Now the premier league's board of directors, chairman Sir John Quinton and newly-appointed chief executive Peter Leaver have been handed the task of settling the issue.
Premier league spokesman John Zarossa said on Tuesday: "We should have a final decision before the end of the week. The board of directors is considering all the arguments from every angle."
The row between the managers escalated on Saturday when Ferguson accused Wenger of unfairly trying to influence premier league bosses.
Wenger said it would be unfair to change the dates now -- and that left Ferguson fuming.
"He has no experience of English football," Ferguson said. "He's been managing in Japan and now he's telling everybody in England how to organise their football.

"Unless you've been in a situation like we were a few years ago, where we had to play four games in eight days -- in the league and in Europe and the cups -- then you should keep your mouth shut, firmly shut," he said.
